title: Championships: NBA and WNBA eras
text:
Takeaways




NBA playoffs punish threes and rim attempts. Points per three-point attempt fell in the playoffs in all 23 seasons (−0.040 points per shot). Rim attempts fell in 87% of seasons. Mid-range shots held up best.
WNBA playoffs show no reliable shot-zone penalty. Every zone’s 95% interval includes zero; with 8-12 playoff teams a year the sample is small.
The WNBA is about six years behind the NBA on the three-point shift, and the gap has grown. In 2026, 37% of WNBA shots were threes, about where the NBA was in 2019-20. In 2017-2020 the gap was about three years.
Recent WNBA champions are ahead of their own league. From 2022 to 2026 they took 5 percentage points more of their shots from three, and 7.5 points fewer at the rim, than the league average. NBA champions have stayed within 3 points of their league.
Everything on this page is association, not causation, and each league is measured against itself.

title: Which player archetypes drive winning, and does pay track that value?
text:
What this project does

Measures every player per possession, with small samples pulled toward their position’s average (empirical Bayes), instead of per-36 numbers that overrate short stints.
Groups players into style archetypes (clustering on shot diet, creation, rebounding and defense), then checks the labels against hand labels and against how players change roles after trades.
Links team archetype mix to winning: net rating, playoff resilience and championships, and how the winning formula has drifted from era to era in each league.
Asks whether pay follows value: salary as a share of the cap, compared within contract types (rookie scale, minimum, max), with intervals. A player is called over- or under-paid only when the interval excludes zero.


Everything here is association, not causation. The WNBA sample is small (12-13 teams a season), so WNBA estimates carry wide intervals. Pages marked in progress will fill in as each step finishes.

K-Means baseline, Gaussian mixtures, BIC + bootstrap stability for k

agreement with blind hand labels, Cohen’s kappa, ARI


Concept drift
pooled vs per-era fits; rolling-window coefficients


Time-aware cross-validation
forward-chained seasons for net rating and title models


Gradient boosting + SHAP
net-rating model and feature importance


Calibration, uncertainty
bootstrap intervals; probability on the eventual champion


Text preprocessing, TF-IDF, embeddings, topic models, zero-shot labels
